I wonder how they have all these good reviews if we've only encountered unhappy people there. We, first and foremost, had a terrifying experience. You only think about the money (and I'll start by saying that fortunately we don't mind spending it), you have no empathy, love, care, or attention for our family members we entrust to you. Yes, because when we entrust an animal to you, we're entrusting part of our family to you. I firmly believe that if we had changed clinics before leaving our Anastasia with you for 48 hours, she would still be here with us. To anyone reading this review, RUN AWAY. PS: They were supposed to refund me €200 because I had paid an amount I didn't owe, but since we then took our kitten away, it took them 17 days. 17 DAYS. There are people who can live off that €200 for a month. But when you walk into that room with your sick kitten, the doctors only talk about MONEY. This costs so much, we do this but it costs so much, and first of all, we have never asked for costs, only for help. Shame on you.

I scheduled an eye exam for my 13-year-old golden retriever's eye problem. On the day of the appointment, he was having balance issues and a slight head tilt. After a very thorough examination, the ophthalmologist requested a neurological evaluation. The neurologist found neurological issues, such as vestibular and/or cerebral palsy. During the exam, she asked us if his gums were always so pale, and we replied that nothing was different. She then listened to his pulse, which was 64, and was still unsure, even though the dog had always been under control and had always been hiking and taking long walks. Just to be safe, she asked if she could come downstairs for a moment and have him checked out at the emergency room, and of course we said yes. When she came back up, she told us she'd had complete blood tests, including coagulation, and a fast ultrasound. Personally, I was perplexed because I expected at least to be consulted. She had had the tests done last month and they were all perfect. During the visit, I had also told her that the dog always had all the routine checkups and had no problems. When she returned, she told us to come back the next day for an emergency MRI with contrast, but since we were leaving for Arezzo, I replied that if I saw any worsening, I would take her to the clinic in Arezzo. She said she would contact us the next day to give us feedback on the tests, but I never heard from anyone again, and for the test report (which was perfect for a 13-year-old dog, by the way) I waited 45 minutes on the phone.
The whole thing ended with a €450 bill because, obviously, the ultrasound and all the tests more than doubled the bill. The dog recovered from the neurological issue within 5 days, which was likely vestibular syndrome. I found this approach truly unethical. Saying, "I'll take the dog down to the emergency room for a moment, just to be on the safe side, and then having him do tests and an ultrasound scan without asking, I found it truly unfair. If she had asked me, I would have shown her the previous month's tests. It confirms that these clinics' goal these days is to bill and have as many tests as possible done to increase the bill and cash in. It's a negative experience I won't repeat. Ethics come first for me. Nowadays, the clinics that are part of these international networks have become nothing but a money-eating machine that takes precedence over everything else. I could have refused to pay for something I didn't authorize and wasn't asked for. From "I'll take the dog down for a moment, just to be on the safe side," to an ultrasound scan and a complete coagulation profile analysis, there's a huge difference. Never again!

Introduction: I had never taken my cat to a veterinary clinic, and given my experience with them, I realized I should and could have made a move sooner.

About a week ago, I took my 9-year-old cat to the clinic, dying and desperate. I didn't have high hopes, nor did I have a lot of money, having unfortunately been caught completely off guard. The doctor who welcomed me, having seen my cat's condition and my financial resources, drew up a treatment plan for me, including the associated costs (€500 for four days with IVs, medications, and various treatments for the kidney failure she was diagnosed with), and I accepted immediately.
I was completely resigned, given my cat's critical condition, but, day after day, I saw improvements and a professionalism and love that reassured me, explaining everything to me in great detail: from the improvements that, fortunately, were tangible day by day, to the advice on how to best care for my cat within the agreed-upon costs.
Finally, after four days of being called once a day to keep me updated on the cat's medical condition, I brought her home, and she's now undergoing medication treatment under the same doctor.
As you can see from the story, they were extremely serious, doing their best to treat my cat, within the limits of my financial resources, and NEVER trying to go beyond that.
The cat's home today is thanks to them and the doctor who treated me.

Dr. Jessica Mega, with an accurate and targeted diagnosis, identified the true origin of the problem in a completely different area of ​​the body. Combined with the excellent work of the technician Aurora, who followed him through the physiotherapy, hydrotherapy, and ozone therapy program, the results arrived in a very short time.
​Just thirty days after changing his therapy, Columbus has returned to a normal life and is walking independently!
​A department of excellence where diagnostic ability, technical expertise, and great empathy for animals truly make a difference. Thank you so much! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We hospitalized our one-year-old German Shepherd for severe kidney failure. After about two weeks of hospitalization, dialysis, transfusions, and nearly €15,000 in expenses, our dog never returned home from that clinic.

He died a few weeks later, with a clinical picture that also included an infection we had repeatedly reported and for which we continued to demand an explanation.

Poor communication, enormous difficulty reaching anyone, utterly rude receptionists, virtually nonexistent empathy, and, in our case, even the treatment by a couple of doctors—whom I choose not to name—that I found professionally disconcerting.

One of them, just as we were insisting on answers about the infection and the dog's condition, had an emotional breakdown, citing her own stress and excessive work hours. A frankly surreal scene at a time when we needed clarity, expertise, and answers.

One thing, however, always arrived promptly: updated costs and estimates.

I would never entrust my pet to this facility again.

If I could do it again, I would never enter this clinic.

On November 13, 2025, we admitted our one-year-old German Shepherd for sudden, severe kidney failure. This was followed by dialysis, transfusions, about two weeks of hospitalization, and a total cost of nearly €15,000.

We did everything we were asked to do because we wanted to save him at all costs.

Unfortunately, our dog never returned home and died on December 28.

During this journey, we experienced a situation I would describe as inhumane: constant difficulty receiving information, unanswered phone calls, a lack of clarity, and above all, very little empathy.

We had also repeatedly reported the presence of what we believed to be an infection and continued to ask for explanations as to what was happening. At one point, a veterinarian, faced with our insistent requests for clarification, broke down emotionally, explaining that she was severely stressed from working too many hours.

I understand the fatigue, but a family with a seriously ill dog needs clear-headed, present, and communicative professionals.

Paradoxically, what was never lacking was punctuality in updating the cost estimates.

We lost a one-year-old dog, and we were left with, in addition to the pain, the memory of weeks of anguish during which we too often felt alone and unheard.

It was a terrifying experience. Personally, I would never go back and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.

We arrived at the clinic on July 28 with the cat that fell from the fourth floor. They kept her there for two days, administering all the necessary treatments and checkups (in their opinion), which cost a whopping €950. They released her with a diagnosis of pulmonary contusion and a course of antibiotics and anti-inflammatory drugs to continue over the next few days.
Unfortunately, the day after she started taking the medications, the cat began to feel sick: vomiting, diarrhea, and not eating or drinking. So we decided to take her back. We stayed from 9:00 AM to 1:15 PM, where she was released again, as deemed appropriate by the doctor in question. After performing a complete blood count, an anti-vomiting medication, and administering something to stimulate her appetite, we were also told to continue with the previously administered treatment and add this appetite-reducing medication, along with a gastroprotective medication. We also pointed out that the dosages prescribed may have been incorrect for the cat's weight, and we were told that the doctor deemed this appropriate. So what are you doing, you don't trust me?? But something was definitely wrong. It's impossible for me to tell you that the cat isn't drinking, eating, or even giving her an IV. Anyway, we decided to take her home anyway because that's what was recommended, and otherwise we would have had to take her the next day for yet another abdominal ultrasound. We also paid €130 for this visit.
The cat, having returned home, is now suffering from diarrhea, after taking both antibiotics and gastroprotective medication. We decide to take her back... and then hell breaks loose because from 2:00 AM to 5:30 AM, they didn't even consider us, or take us into consideration. After paying a fortune and having nothing resolved, without receiving any information about the dosage, we were thrown into that waiting room with no one, I repeat, no doctor or nurse outside the reception desk... because last night's problem was also the reception desk, with the computers not working.
So I ask myself... what are the emergencies for you?
We left, after knocking on the door a thousand times and asking to speak to someone, exhausted and tired, because like them, we too were coming off a day at work... we decided to take her to our vet today, August 3rd, as soon as they opened. And guess what: the antibiotic and anti-inflammatory dosages were too high for the cat's weight; they were superficial and unprofessional. And they still haven't given us any answers, even after paying so much.
You should be truly ashamed, because that's not how you behave or relate.
Hire more staff if you don't know how to manage the facility.
No more wintering.

AniCura Veterinary Clinic, South Rome

I'd like everyone to read this review. I entrusted my dog, Sirio, to this clinic, believing I was leaving him in the hands of professionals. Unfortunately, the experience was devastating.

The first thing that deeply affected me was Dr. Pollina's attitude. After waiting for over three hours with my dog ​​on a stretcher, and after I pointed out that people who had arrived after me had been seen first, I was told, "Let's schedule the appointments first." In a facility that bills itself as a veterinary emergency room, such a response is, in my opinion, unacceptable.

Sirio subsequently visited Dr. Morales for severe neurological symptoms. The following day, at another clinic, he was diagnosed with extremely high blood pressure. There, I was told that such high blood pressure would need to be stabilized before administering anesthesia, as it would pose a significant risk.

Dr. Morales's report does not include any blood pressure readings. As far as I can see in the documentation in my possession, this parameter was neither reported nor documented. I subsequently received a summary sheet stating that the dog was "normal blood pressure." This statement left me deeply perplexed, as I am not aware that his blood pressure was ever measured during that visit.

I requested clarification on this point. I received an apology from the health director and other professionals at the facility for the inconsistencies found in the documentation, but not from the doctor who treated Sirio.
I cannot say with certainty that Sirio would have survived, because no one can know. However, I can say that I expected greater caution, greater attention to the clinical assessment, and clearer and more transparent communication at such a delicate time.

I am writing this review not out of revenge. I also encountered well-trained and helpful professionals at the center, but I believe that anyone who entrusts their pet to a veterinary facility has the right to receive thorough care, precise clinical documentation, and accurate information.

Unfortunately, Sirio fell into the wrong hands with Dr. MORALES.
